## Project conventions for this repo
This project has two codelines — mocka at /home/bradleyjerome/projects/mock3/mock-a and mockb at /home/bradleyjerome/projects/mock3/mock-b. Each is a standalone npm package with its own package.json, tsconfig.json, src/, and test/ directory; there is no monorepo root. The story you are assigned names its codeline; work only within that codeline's root.

- **Language**: TypeScript, strict mode. tsconfig.json sets "strict": true, "moduleResolution": "bundler", "target": "ES2022", "module": "ES2022", "include": ["src", "test"]. Use ESM import/export — never CommonJS require. Both codelines declare "type": "module" in package.json.
- **Test runner**: vitest 2.x, invoked as `npm test` (which runs `vitest run`). There is no vitest config file; vitest uses defaults and picks up test/*.test.ts automatically. Tests import source as `import { ... } from '../src/<module>'`.
- **Type-check / build**: `npm run build` runs `tsc --noEmit`. This typechecks both src/ and test/. Both `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before a change is accepted.
- **No lockfile**: neither codeline has a lockfile. Dependencies are declared in package.json devDependencies only (vitest, typescript). No other runtime or framework is declared — do not assume any dependency that does not appear in the codeline's own manifest.
- **Source layout**: source lives under src/, tests under test/. The implementer role (typescript-bugfix-engineer) edits source files only — never test files. A separate agent owns all test authorship. If you believe a test is missing, say so in your report and stop; do not create or edit any file under test/.
- **Minimal changes**: both tickets in this project are single-operator or single-bound fixes. Do not refactor surrounding code. If a caller of the function you change appears to depend on the current (incorrect) behavior, stop and report it rather than working around it.
